content: The process of scaling up the use of red blood cell folate measurements in national surveys presents challenges, particularly in terms of the resources required to standardize methodologies across different laboratories. This includes ensuring the use of appropriate microbiological assay techniques, training skilled personnel, and acquiring necessary equipment. The extent of these resource requirements remains unclear. Establishing surveillance systems for neural tube defects also incurs significant costs. While improving laboratory capacity and surveillance systems is achievable, it necessitates coordinated efforts among stakeholders and sufficient financial resources. However, such resources may be limited in lowand middle-income countries. The WHO guideline on optimal serum and red blood cell folate concentrations in women of reproductive age for the prevention of neural tube defects was developed with input from various experts. The WHO steering committee included Dr. Luz Maria De-Regil, an epidemiologist specializing in evidence and program guidance in nutrition for health and development; Dr. Mario Merialdi, a coordinator in reproductive health research; and Dr. Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas, a coordinator in nutrition for health and development. The guideline development group included experts such as Dr. Daniel J. Raiten from the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, specializing in endocrinology, nutrition, and growth; Dr. Irma Silva-Zolezzi from Nestlé Research Center, focusing on nutrition and health; Dr. Joseph Sniezek from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), specializing in birth defects and developmental disabilities; Dr. Mary Serdula from the CDC, focusing on nutrition, physical activity, and obesity; Dr. Kevin Sullivan from Emory University, specializing in epidemiology; and Ms. Aliki Pappas Weakland from the CDC, focusing on birth defects and developmental disabilities. Content expert peer reviewers included Dr. Pierpaolo Mastroiacovo from the Alessandra Lisi International Centre on Birth Defects and Prematurity in Rome, Italy; Dr. María Elizabeth Tejero Barrera from the National Institute of Genomic Medicine in Mexico City, specializing in nutrigenetics and nutrigenomics; and Dr. Mindy Zhang from the CDC’s Global Micronutrient Laboratory, focusing on nutritional biomarkers. External reviewers, selected through a public call for comments, included Dr. Cutberto Espinosa Lopez from the Ministry of Health in Mexico, specializing in epidemiology; Ms. Michelle Gibbs from the Ministry for Primary Industries in New Zealand, focusing on bioscience, food science, and risk assessment; Dr. Vijaya Kancherla from Emory University, specializing in spina bifida research and prevention; and Dr. Guillermo Melendez from Hospital General de México.
